title: Top exterior power of a direct sum
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ and $N$ be free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with bases of $r$ and $s$ elements, and write $\bigwedge^n$ for the $n$-th exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. The alternating map sending $(m_1\wedge\cdots\wedge m_r)\otimes(n_1\wedge\cdots\wedge n_s)$ to $(m_1,0)\wedge\cdots\wedge(m_r,0)\wedge(0,n_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(0,n_s)$ induces a canonical $R$-module isomorphism $\bigwedge^{r+s}(M\oplus N)\cong\bigwedge^rM\otimes_R\bigwedge^sN$, where the tensor product is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], natural in isomorphisms of $M$ and $N$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: Construct the canonical linear map from the tensor product to the (r+s)-th exterior power: apply exterior-power maps of the two inclusions into M × N and multiply in the exterior algebra. The graded multiplication places the product in degree r+s. TensorProduct.lift supplies the linear map. ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_mul_ιMulti proves the concatenated-wedge formula for every pair of tuples, without choosing bases.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: For a basis indexed by Fin n, reindex its n-th exterior-power basis by Unit: the sole subset of size n is the full set. Its increasing enumeration is the identity, since a strictly increasing endomap of a finite linear order is the identity. Thus the single basis vector is the wedge of the original basis. Reindex the product basis of M × N along finSumFinEquiv to obtain the concatenated basis. Tensor the two one-element exterior-power bases. By the wedge formula, the constructed linear map agrees on this tensor basis with the linear equivalence to the single concatenated wedge basis. It is therefore bijective; its inverse is the required isomorphism.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: TensorProduct.ext and two applications of exteriorPower.linearMap_ext show that linear maps out of the tensor product are determined by pure tensors of pure wedges. Apply this to the inverse of any isomorphism with the characterization to prove uniqueness. For naturality, compare exteriorPower.map composed with the first inverse with the second inverse composed with TensorProduct.map. On pure tensors of wedges their equality follows from both characterizations, map_apply_ιMulti, map_tmul, and the fact that the product map commutes with the two inclusions. Extensionality proves equality everywhere. Evaluate at e x and use injectivity of the second inverse to obtain the stated orientation.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_topDirectSum {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (r s : ℕ) (_bM : Module.Basis (Fin r) R M) (_bN : Module.Basis (Fin s) R N) : ∃! e : (⋀[R]^(r + s) (M × N)) ≃ₗ[R] ((⋀[R]^r M) ⊗[R] (⋀[R]^s N)), ∀ (m : Fin r → M) (n : Fin s → N), e.symm ((ιMulti R r m) ⊗ₜ[R] (ιMulti R s n)) = ιMulti R (r + s) (Fin.append (fun i ↦ (m i, 0)) (fun j ↦ (0, n j)))
lean.note: The first theorem gives the unique isomorphism characterized by its inverse on pure wedges; the second states naturality for every pair of isomorphisms and every two isomorphisms with that characterization. The binary module direct sum is represented by its standard product model.
